calc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
calc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

calc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
calc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

calc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
calc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

hw.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.
hw.translation_notes: 'Head' in the hydraulic sense (energy per unit weight) does not translate literally in many languages — use the established civil/hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'gubitak pritiska' (= pressure loss), which is technically the same concept expressed in pressure terms rather than head terms. The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ro/tr/id translations were pressure-loss-sense ('pierdere de presiune'/'basınç kaybı'/'kehilangan tekanan'), contradicting this note's own guidance. Independently flagged by both the ro and tr wave-1 translation agents; corrected to head-loss-sense ('pierdere de sarcină'/'yük kaybı'/'kehilangan tinggi tekan') to match what both agents actually used in lib/lang.ec.ro.php and lib/lang.ec.tr.php. de's 'Druckverlust' was left as-is (not flagged; German engineering practice uses pressure/head loss terms more interchangeably in pipe-flow context) but is worth a second look in a future audit. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 fa sprint): fa was 'افت فشار' (literally 'pressure loss', same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id fix above), while the fa file's own mphl_ head-loss labels already used 'افت هد' (head loss) and 'هد' is an established loanword elsewhere in the file (هد سرعت = velocity head). Standardized to 'افت هد' suite-wide for fa and fixed dw_/hw_ labels in lib/lang.ec.fa.php to match. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): glossary sw value was 'upotevu wa shinikizo' (= pressure loss), the same pressure-loss-sense defect class as the ro/tr/id/fa fixes above. But lib/lang.ec.sw.php's own dw_main_desc/dw_main_menu/dw_main_title/mphl_main_desc/mphl_main_menu/mphl_main_title (and mpf_velocity_head, ws_headWaterHeight, or_head, mhp_gross_head elsewhere in the file) all already establish 'Kichwa' (head) as the suite's real Swahili word for hydraulic head, not 'shinikizo' (pressure). Standardized the glossary to 'upotevu wa kichwa' to match the file's own established, correct usage instead of the stale pressure-sense glossary value. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 ps wave-3 sprint): glossary ps value was 'د سر زیان' (زیان = damage/loss), but lib/lang.ec.ps.php's own dw_/hw_/mpf_/mphl_ head-loss labels (40+ occurrences suite-wide) all already use ضیاع, not زیان, for 'loss' (e.g. existing dw_main_menu 'Darcy-Weisbach د پایپ سر ضیاع', mphl_total_loss). زیان does not occur anywhere in the file. Standardized the glossary to 'د سر ضیاع' to match the file's actual established usage, same defect class as the sw fix above. Task 109 stages 4-5 (2026-07-19): am confirmed on ሄድ (the ጭንቅ 'distress' mistranslation of 'head' was corrected suite-wide in this category); sw 'loss' must be Upotevu, not Hasara (financial loss) — fixed in ip_group_loss. | [2026-07-20] Stage-6 ur audit found the glossary's own value (ہیڈ لاس, a transliteration) was outdated; corrected to دباؤ نقصان, the suite incumbent used 9x across dw_/hw_/mphl_ and now applied in mhp_ for consistency.

mtc.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): previous sw value 'radius ya maji' (literally 'radius of water', English loanword 'radius' + 'of water') named the substance rather than the hydraulic-geometry property, and did not read as an engineering term. Changed to 'radiasi ya kihaidroliki' (radius + 'hydraulic', adjectival ki- form), matching the '[radius] + hydraulic' construction used by fr/de/it/es/ro/tr (rayon hydraulique / hydraulischer Radius / raggio idraulico / radio hidráulico / raza hidraulică / hidrolik yarıçap). Used in lib/lang.ec.sw.php's mpf_hydraulic_radius.

mtc.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use. Task 109 stages 4 & 5 (2026-07-19): bg wrong-word 'навлажнен' (moistened) corrected to 'омокрен' in mpf_wetted_perimeter (stage 4) and cs_notes_3_def (stage 5); km គ្រែទឹក (water bed) also confirmed corrected to glossary បរិវេណសើម (stage 4).

mtc.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mtc.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'.
